description: Hooks of this eca: aos functions run when an event happens. eca has before_queue, after_queue, brain_failed (CliFailed / ReplyMissing) and tool_added and on_clock in aos-eca-turn, after_start / after_stop and before_run / after_run (before / after each turn) from loop.json, and before_tool / after_tool only for aos tools called through aos-mcp; before_compact / after_compact around Claude Code's own compaction come from compact_hook (wired in cli.json settings: before_compact can change the summary instructions, give restore text for after the compaction, or block; after_compact only tells, with the summary); the CLI's own tools and what a person types on the screen are not seen. brain_notify sends BLOCKED letters to AOS_NOTIFY_BOX when a claude turn fails after hand-over (from the third retry of a temporary API error, or when it stops); codex events are ignored. The stack copy of this file overrides it by name, null turns one off. self_hook is not in this eca's tools (its events pack is not stacked since 11-22): add it first with self_tools {"op": "add", "path_json": {"$env": "AOS_HOME", "$path": "/lib/tools/agent/self_hook"}}. screen_linger_start cancels pending screen closures; screen_linger_stop closes screens after cli.json screen_close_after_s seconds (default 600, 0 immediately). Setting both to null leaves screens open indefinitely. The timer hook is a place to hang something every 5 minutes (on_clock, every_ms 300000, AOS_CLOCK); its handler does nothing. The mail_notify hook looks at your mailbox every minute (on_clock, every_ms 60000) and, only when new letters came, puts one message "[aos] new_mail: N new letters from A, B. ..." in your queue (after a sleep, letters that came while you slept are announced once, those announced before are not; on a fresh start (no notified.json and no non-empty history.jsonl yet) waiting letters are only marked as known; a stack that already ran (has non-empty history) is treated like waking up: waiting letters are announced once); turn it off or change the interval in your stack copy (self_hook rm / add with replace). The context_wrap hook looks every 5 seconds at how full your context is (input tokens of the last call of the last finished turn / the context window; brains that give no reading are left alone): at or over config percent (default 35) it puts one message "[aos] context_wrap: ... Wrap up now ..." in your queue, and once that is answered and the queue is empty it sends a letter that is only /compact (always a batch of its own); it does not repeat until a later reading is under the limit again. Change the limit in config.percent of this entry (here, or a same-named entry in the stack copy of this file; self_hook add with replace and config sets it), or turn it off with self_hook rm.
